sources.title: First offers as anchors: The role of perspective-taking and negotiator focus
sources.setting: Three simulated buyer-seller bargaining experiments, including face-to-face and email conditions; detailed sample recruitment not checked.
sources.finding: First offers influenced settlement prices; focusing on one's target or the counterpart's alternatives or reservation price removed the first-offer advantage in these experiments.
sources.use: Before drafting a salary request, separate supported market comparisons, personal target, alternatives and unknown employer constraints. Treat a prepared range as a proposal, not an entitlement.
limits: Simulated distributive bargaining is not a Chinese hiring field trial.
No always-go-first rule, arbitrary anchor, guaranteed raise or personal success probability follows.
sources.jurisdiction: Research context; no legal jurisdiction or direct China-specific validation established.
sources.version: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 81(4), 657-669; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.81.4.657. Abstract checked; full methods not read.

sources.title: Social incentives for gender differences in the propensity to initiate negotiations: Sometimes it does hurt to ask
sources.authors: Hannah Riley Bowles; Linda Babcock; Lei Lai
sources.setting: Four compensation scenarios using written or recorded candidates and evaluator judgments; samples included North American students and recruited adults.
sources.finding: Negotiation attempts produced different social evaluations across candidate and evaluator conditions. The observed gender patterns depended on the scenario.
sources.use: Offer several evidence-backed request styles, clarify the organization's negotiation process and let the candidate choose an acceptable approach and fallback.
limits: Scenario evaluations and stated intentions do not establish an individual's real salary outcome.
Do not stereotype a candidate or evaluator by gender, recommend silence because of gender, or promise that softer wording prevents backlash.
No direct validation for contemporary Chinese employers.
sources.jurisdiction: North American research setting; not employment law.
sources.version: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 103(1), 84-103; DOI 10.1016/j.obhdp.2006.09.001. Abstract and methods excerpts checked in Harvard-hosted PDF.

sources.title: 中华人民共和国劳动合同法（2012年修订文本）
sources.authors: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
sources.setting: Official Shanghai human-resources authority reproduction; checked scope and contract-formation provisions, including articles 2 and 8-20.
sources.finding: The text addresses recruitment disclosures, retention of identity documents, written contracts, required contract terms and probation conditions.
sources.use: Compare the actual employer, work location, pay basis, contract duration and probation wording; produce questions and missing documents before acceptance.
limits: Confirm the actual employment relationship, jurisdiction, current amendments and applicable local rules before giving rights advice.
An offer, internship, contractor arrangement or disputed relationship needs separate assessment; do not declare individual liability or compensation from this card.
sources.jurisdiction: Mainland China; statutory employment relationships within article 2, subject to actual facts.
sources.version: The page reproduces the 2012-12-28 amendment and its 2013-07-01 commencement, plus the amended law. This dated reproduction is not a claim that all 2026 legal developments were checked.

sources.title: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法
sources.authors: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
sources.setting: Official market-regulator reproduction; checked articles 3, 6, 13, 17, 28-30 and 44-47.
sources.finding: The text limits collection to necessary purposes, recognizes multiple lawful processing grounds and adds conditions for sensitive information and certain individual rights.
sources.use: Minimize resume data; ask who collects requested information, for what purpose, for how long and through which channel. Redact private documents before sharing with the assistant.
limits: Consent is not the only lawful basis; a request is not automatically unlawful.
Recheck current official rules, processing grounds, exceptions and facts before applying rights or deletion provisions; this card gives no individual legal determination.
sources.jurisdiction: Mainland China processing and article 3's specified extraterritorial circumstances; scope needs fact-specific checking.
sources.version: 2021-08-20 enactment; 2021-11-01 commencement confirmed in the reproduced presidential order. SAMR page dated 2023-04-07; later legal developments not comprehensively checked.

sources.title: 人力资源服务机构管理规定
sources.authors: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of the People's Republic of China
sources.setting: Official Beijing government reproduction of ministry rules; checked scope, licensing and service provisions, including articles 5, 15, 22, 24 and 26-27.
sources.finding: The rules address intermediary licensing, recruitment information, applicant data, complaint mechanisms, disclosed charges and prohibited deposit or coerced-loan practices.
sources.use: For an intermediary, identify its legal entity, check relevant licensing through official records and distinguish job recruitment from paid training or lending.
limits: A job advertisement or licence alone does not establish safety; employment agencies and direct employers have different obligations.
Recheck current official rules and local supervision channels; do not infer a criminal offence or reimbursement entitlement.
sources.jurisdiction: Mainland China human-resources service institutions within the rules' scope.
sources.version: MOHRSS Order 50, announced 2023-06-29 and effective 2023-08-01, as stated in the reproduced rule heading; do not confuse the page metadata date with commencement or claim an exhaustive 2026 law check.

sources.title: @找工作的你，警惕“招转培”“招转贷”！
sources.authors: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security; reproduced by the State Council client
sources.setting: Official jobseeker warning about recruitment being redirected into training fees, equipment purchases or loans.
sources.finding: The warning describes high-pay recruitment bait followed by paid-training or lending demands and directs affected jobseekers to preserve evidence and approach appropriate authorities.
sources.use: When payment or borrowing becomes an entry condition, pause the transaction, preserve the advertisement and agreements, verify the parties independently and consult the relevant official channel.
limits: Pattern similarity is a warning signal, not proof of fraud or a ruling on an existing loan.
Reopen current official guidance before advising; do not tell a user to ignore repayment, promise recovery or confront a suspected scammer.
sources.jurisdiction: Mainland China job-search context; competent agencies depend on the facts and location.
sources.version: Dated official warning published 2025-06-11; educational guidance, not legislation or a complete statement of current remedies.
